questions.question: Which of the following correctly synthesizes the chapter's framework by matching each term of the iron law of ML performance ($T = D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW} + O/(R_{\text{peak}} \cdot \eta_{\text{hw}}) + L_{\text{lat}}$) to its primary performance engineering intervention?
choices: Data movement ($D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW}$) is reduced by CUDA Graphs; overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$) is eliminated by INT4 quantization; compute ($O/R_{\text{peak}}$) is restructured by increasing GPU clock speed

Data movement ($D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW}$) is reduced by speculative decoding; overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$) is eliminated by FlashAttention; compute ($O/R_{\text{peak}}$) is restructured by adding more InfiniBand cables

Data movement ($D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW}$) is reduced by FlashAttention and INT4/INT8 quantization; overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$) is eliminated by CUDA Graphs and communication overlap; compute ($O/R_{\text{peak}}$) is restructured by speculative decoding and MoE
Data movement ($D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW}$) is reduced by increasing batch size; overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$) is eliminated by MoE; compute ($O/R_{\text{peak}}$) is restructured by disabling Python GIL
questions.answer: The correct answer is C. Data movement ($D_{\text{vol}}/\text{BW}$) is reduced by FlashAttention and INT4/INT8 quantization; overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$) is eliminated by CUDA Graphs and communication overlap; compute ($O/R_{\text{peak}}$) is restructured by speculative decoding and MoE. The chapter structures all performance techniques around the three terms of the iron law. FlashAttention (tiling to SRAM) and quantization (INT4 weights, INT8 KV cache) shrink the exposed bytes moved ($D_{\text{vol}}$). Graph compilers (`torch.compile`), CUDA Graphs, and asynchronous communication overlap eliminate launch latency, dispatch gaps, and exposed network wait ($L_{\text{lat}}$). Algorithmic transformations like speculative decoding and MoE change the intrinsic computational work ($O$) required to emit tokens. The alternative pairings misclassify technique targets across the governing equation.
questions.learning_objective: Synthesize the chapter's performance engineering taxonomy by mapping optimization techniques to their corresponding terms in the iron law

questions.question: What is the central unifying thesis of performance engineering in modern machine learning systems?
choices: Performance engineering is the practice of replacing all high-level framework code with raw assembly instructions regardless of measured profiling bottlenecks
Peak advertised FLOP/s is the sole determinant of end-to-end model speed, so optimization should focus exclusively on maximizing Tensor Core clock frequencies
Any optimization that accelerates distributed training will automatically deliver identical percentage speedups for single-user interactive inference

Hardware throughput is fundamentally constrained by physical limits (the memory wall, launch latency, and interconnect bandwidth); performance engineering systematically matches software execution to hardware physics by reducing data movement, eliminating overhead, and adapting algorithms to hardware balance points
questions.answer: The correct answer is D. Hardware throughput is fundamentally constrained by physical limits (the memory wall, launch latency, and interconnect bandwidth); performance engineering systematically matches software execution to hardware physics by reducing data movement, eliminating overhead, and adapting algorithms to hardware balance points. Accelerators provide massive theoretical arithmetic peak ($R_{\text{peak}}$), but real execution is bounded by data movement costs across the memory hierarchy (pJ/byte and HBM bandwidth), software dispatch overhead ($L_{\text{lat}}$), and interconnect delays. Performance engineering is the disciplined application of measurement, diagnosis, and hardware-aware transformations (fusion, precision, compilation, overlap, and algorithmic restructuring) to close the gap between silicon peak and realized throughput. The other choices represent discredited dogmas (blind assembly rewriting, FLOP/s obsession, or conflating training with inference regimes).
questions.learning_objective: Articulate the unifying principle of hardware-software co-design and physics-guided optimization in ML systems

questions.question: Why does the chapter emphasize that performance profiling must be treated as an iterative, continuous loop throughout an engineering project rather than a one-time initial measurement?
choices: Because performance optimization is a waterbed problem: resolving the primary bottleneck (e.g., slashing weight reads with INT4) shifts execution to a new binding constraint (e.g., element-wise launch gaps or compute saturation), requiring fresh diagnosis for subsequent gains
Because GPU hardware counters change their physical definitions after every kernel execution
Because graph compilers require fresh profiling traces on every iteration to prevent HBM memory leaks
Because initial profiling measurements are always 100% inaccurate due to the Heisenberg effect
questions.answer: The correct answer is A. Because performance optimization is a waterbed problem: resolving the primary bottleneck (e.g., slashing weight reads with INT4) shifts execution to a new binding constraint (e.g., element-wise launch gaps or compute saturation), requiring fresh diagnosis for subsequent gains. As demonstrated by the 70B case study, optimization is bottleneck displacement. In Round 1, INT4 quantization solved the HBM bandwidth wall and enabled larger batches, which pushed the system into an element-wise and launch-bound regime. Round 2 addressed this with `torch.compile` and FlashAttention, exposing the next opportunity for speculative decoding in Round 3. Attempting to apply Round 2 or Round 3 techniques without reprofiling leads to misdirected effort on non-binding terms. Profiling is not just the first step; it is every step. The other choices invent absurd counter redefinitions, compiler leak myths, or overstate profiling perturbation.
questions.learning_objective: Evaluate why continuous, iterative reprofiling is essential to navigate shifting bottleneck regimes in performance engineering
